pages.title: Services
pages.content:
Services foropen sites

Daichi Landscapes plants, builds roofs and planters, and returns for aftercare on campuses, hospitals and civic streets in Metro Vancouver. The four services below are the work we schedule from the yard.

01

Tree & street planting

Street tree planting starts at $680 CAD per tree. The price includes the guard and 2 seasons of watering. We set each tree in a pit measured at the site survey, on campuses, hospital edges and civic streets across Metro Vancouver. Priya Raman, arborist, checks the species, the stake and the clearance before the pit is closed.

Tom Okafor leads the planting crew. The Northshore College forecourt in 2024 took 64 trees and 1,800 m² of planting. Fraser Street renewal in 2025 took 112 street trees along 1.2 km. A site survey and planting plan, from $1,200 CAD, is how either kind of job begins.

from $680 CAD · per tree

02

Campus grounds

Campus grounds maintenance starts at $3,400 CAD per month, for grounds up to 2 ha. The monthly work keeps beds, edges and irrigation in order while the campus stays open to the people who use it. Riverside General Hospital, completed in 2023, is the hospital example: 3 courtyards and a sensory garden, with benches and grasses kept under the same aftercare record.

Hana Mori-Ellis writes the planting plan. Marcus Delgado, operations lead, sets the crew schedule around the life of the site. The monthly price is a starting figure. The survey confirms the area before the first month is booked.

from $3,400 CAD · per month

03

Green roofs & planters

Green roof and planter installation starts at $145 CAD per m². Elise Brandt leads irrigation and green roofs. The work puts soil, a drainage layer and a watering line into planters and onto low roofs where a campus or hospital has little open ground left.

We do not order soil until the site survey and planting plan are written. That survey and plan start at $1,200 CAD. The same two planting policies apply here as on a street: 60% native or adapted species in the plan, and 80% of stock grown within 150 km. Aftercare on a planting contract still runs 24 months.

from $145 CAD · per m²

04

Seasonal aftercare

Seasonal aftercare is the close of every planting contract, and it runs for 24 months. A seasonal aftercare visit starts at $420 CAD. Samuel Quist, aftercare coordinator, sets the visits, watches the 2 seasons of watering that come with a street tree, and calls the crew when a stake or a cut needs a return.

Winter pruning starts at $1,950 CAD per day for a crew of 3, with Priya Raman directing the work. Aftercare is priced as a visit or as a pruning day. It is not folded quietly into the planting price.

from $420 CAD · per visit

Starting prices

Starting prices

Six starting prices cover the work we are asked for most often. All are in CAD. Site survey and planting plan, from $1,200. Street tree planting, per tree, including the guard and 2 seasons of watering, from $680. Campus grounds maintenance, per month, up to 2 ha, from $3,400. Green roof and planter install, per m², from $145. Seasonal aftercare visit, from $420. Winter pruning, per day, for a crew of 3, from $1,950. These are starting prices. The survey sets quantities, and the written plan is what we plant to. Winter planting slots for 2027 are open for survey bookings now.

See the full price list →

Sustainability

What we hold to on every plan

Three figures are company policy on every planting plan, not a slogan for one project. 80% of planting stock is grown within 150 km. 60% of the species in each plan are native or adapted. Aftercare runs 24 months on every planting contract. We use the same three figures on a college forecourt, a hospital courtyard and a civic street. The case records sit beside them. Northshore College shows 62 of 64 trees established after 24 months. Riverside General Hospital shows 3 of 3 courtyards. Fraser Street shows 109 of 112 street trees.

pages.title: Pricing
pages.content:
Six startingprices in CAD

Starting prices are in Canadian dollars and match the six rates used across Daichi Landscapes. A site survey turns each rate into a measured quantity.

Six starting prices

Every price below is a starting price in CAD, confirmed after the site survey. Site survey and planting plan: $1,200. Street tree planting, per tree: $680. Campus grounds maintenance, per month, up to 2 ha: $3,400. Green roof and planter install, per m²: $145. Seasonal aftercare visit: $420. Winter pruning, per day, crew of 3: $1,950. We publish the six figures so a facilities lead can see the shape of a job before week 1. The survey, in weeks 1–2, is what turns a starting price into a quantity. Hana Mori-Ellis writes the plan that follows, in weeks 3–5.

Survey, plan and street trees

The $1,200 CAD starting price covers the site survey and the planting plan. In weeks 1–2 we measure pits, paving edges and the room each tree needs. In weeks 3–5 the plan is written, including the rule of 60% native or adapted species and the rule that 80% of stock is grown within 150 km. Street tree planting starts at $680 CAD per tree.

That tree price includes the guard and 2 seasons of watering. It does not include the survey. Tom Okafor leads planting in weeks 9–11. Priya Raman checks stake and clearance on the street trees before handover.

Campus grounds and green roofs

Campus grounds maintenance starts at $3,400 CAD per month and applies to grounds up to 2 ha. It is the monthly care of a campus, hospital courtyard or similar ground after planting, scheduled by Marcus Delgado so the site can stay in use. Riverside General Hospital, with 3 courtyards and a sensory garden, is the kind of ground this price refers to.

Green roof and planter install starts at $145 CAD per m². Elise Brandt leads that work: soil, drainage and irrigation on roofs and in planters. Both prices are starting points. Area, in hectares or in m², comes from the survey.

Aftercare visits and winter pruning

A seasonal aftercare visit starts at $420 CAD. Samuel Quist coordinates these visits across the 24 months written into every planting contract. The visit is the unit. We do not quote the 24 months as a single lump sum on this page.

Winter pruning starts at $1,950 CAD per day for a crew of 3. Priya Raman directs pruning. Use it when a planted campus, courtyard or street needs structural cuts in the dormant season. The 2 seasons of watering included with a street tree at $680 CAD sit inside that tree price, separate from the $420 CAD visit.

What the survey settles

Bring a site, not a guessed count. The survey records pits, areas and access, and the plan names species within the 60% native or adapted policy. Stock is then ordered so that 80% is grown within 150 km. You will see the six starting prices again on the plan as rates, applied to the quantities we measured.

Winter planting slots for 2027 are open. To book a survey, call +1 604 555 0148 or write to hello@daichi-landscapes.example. The yard and office are open Monday to Friday, 7:00–17:00. Saturday 8:00–12:00 is for yard pickups only. Sunday is closed.

Request a site survey →

pages.title: Projects
pages.content:
Projects onthe record

Three Metro Vancouver projects are written up here with the year, the scope and the establishment record after 24 months. Each one started as a site survey.

Three jobs on record

Daichi Landscapes keeps three project records on this page, all in Metro Vancouver, all run through the same six stages from site survey to 24 months of aftercare. They are a college forecourt, a hospital courtyard and a civic street. The facts here are the ones we repeat everywhere: year, scope and trees or courtyards established after 24 months. Hana Mori-Ellis wrote the planting plans. Tom Okafor led planting. Samuel Quist coordinated aftercare. Prices on the pricing page are current starting prices, not reconstructions of these invoices.

College · Metro Vancouver · 2024

Northshore College forecourt

64 trees · 1,800 m²

Northshore College forecourt was planted in 2024. The client is a college, the place is Metro Vancouver, and the scope is 64 trees and 1,800 m² of planting. The forecourt is a campus ground: young trees set into pale paving where people cross between buildings.

The job used our ordinary sequence, from the site survey in weeks 1–2 to the handover walk in week 12, then seasonal aftercare. After 24 months, 62 of 64 trees were established. Priya Raman keeps that establishment figure with the case record. It is the number we cite for this forecourt, unchanged.

Read the case →

Hospital · Metro Vancouver · 2023

Riverside General Hospital courtyard

3 courtyards · sensory garden

Riverside General Hospital courtyard was completed in 2023. The client is a hospital, the place is Metro Vancouver, and the scope is 3 courtyards and a sensory garden. Benches and grasses sit in the courtyards, and the garden is planted for close, everyday use by people on the site.

After 24 months, 3 of 3 courtyards were established. Elise Brandt’s irrigation work and Samuel Quist’s aftercare both ran on this job, because a working hospital courtyard has to be watered and then watched. The record we publish for Riverside is those 3 courtyards, established.

Read the case →

Civic street · Metro Vancouver · 2025

Fraser Street renewal

1.2 km · 112 street trees

Fraser Street renewal was planted in 2025. The client is a civic street, the place is Metro Vancouver, and the scope is 1.2 km and 112 street trees. Trees stand in a renewed street with a planted median, each pit set out from the survey and each guard included in the way we plant street trees.

After 24 months, 109 of 112 street trees were established. That is the case figure for Fraser Street. The street is the clearest view we have of a long run of new trees, one planting contract, one aftercare period.

Read the case →

pages.title: Northshore College forecourt
pages.content:
Northshore Collegeforecourt

In 2024 Daichi Landscapes planted the Northshore College forecourt in Metro Vancouver: 64 trees and 1,800 m². After 24 months, 62 of 64 trees were established.

Case facts

Case facts

Client type: college. Place: Metro Vancouver. Year: 2024. Scope: 64 trees and 1,800 m² of planting. After 24 months, 62 of 64 trees were established. The work was a planting contract, so it included the site survey, the planting plan, ground preparation, planting, the handover walk and seasonal aftercare. Hana Mori-Ellis wrote the plan. Tom Okafor led the planting crew. Priya Raman checked the trees. Samuel Quist coordinated the 24 months that followed week 12. The establishment count, 62 of 64, is the ring we keep on this case.

62 of 64

Established after 24 months

64 trees, 1,800 m²

Planting the forecourt

Northshore College needed a forecourt that would keep working as a campus entrance, with young trees set into paving people actually cross. In 2024 we took the job as an ordinary planting contract. Weeks 1–2 were the site survey: pits, edges and the room each of the 64 trees would need inside 1,800 m² of planting. Weeks 3–5 were the planting plan. Hana Mori-Ellis held the plan to the same two rules we use on every job, 60% native or adapted species and 80% of stock grown within 150 km.

Weeks 6–8 were ground preparation. Weeks 9–11 were planting. Tom Okafor’s crew set the trees, with guards where walking routes pass the pits. Priya Raman checked stake and clearance before each pit was closed. Nothing in the scope was added after the plan. The college got 64 trees and 1,800 m², which is the record.

Handover and the 24 months

Week 12 was the handover walk. College staff walked the forecourt with the crew and took the plan for the next 24 months. Samuel Quist coordinated seasonal aftercare from that week. The forecourt is campus ground, so the monthly care of a ground like this sits in the same family as our campus maintenance work, while the establishment watch sat with aftercare.

At 24 months the case record shows 62 of 64 trees established. We leave the figure as a count of trees, not a percentage and not a promise about the next campus. The two trees outside that count remain part of the same record. People still cross the forecourt between buildings. The young trees are the ones planted in 2024, on the paving measured in weeks 1–2, under a plan that did not change the 64 or the 1,800 m².

pages.title: Riverside General Hospital courtyard
pages.content:
Riverside GeneralHospital courtyard

Riverside General Hospital’s 3 courtyards and sensory garden were completed in 2023 in Metro Vancouver. After 24 months, 3 of 3 courtyards were established.

Case facts

Case facts

Client type: hospital. Place: Metro Vancouver. Year: 2023. Scope: 3 courtyards and a sensory garden. After 24 months, 3 of 3 courtyards were established. The contract ran the six stages we use on every planting job, from the site survey in weeks 1–2 through seasonal aftercare for 24 months. Hana Mori-Ellis wrote the planting plan. Elise Brandt led irrigation. Samuel Quist coordinated aftercare. Marcus Delgado scheduled the crew around a hospital that stayed open. The establishment record on this case is the courtyards: 3 of 3.

3 of 3

Established after 24 months

3 courtyards, sensory garden

Three courtyards and a sensory garden

Riverside General Hospital asked for 3 courtyards and a sensory garden, and the work was completed in 2023. The courtyards hold benches and grasses. The garden is for people who use the hospital at close range, so the planting had to be readable by touch, scent and sight without asking the building to change how it runs. Weeks 1–2 were the survey of the three spaces. Weeks 3–5 were the plan.

Hana Mori-Ellis applied the same policies as on a street: 60% native or adapted species, and 80% of stock grown within 150 km. Weeks 6–8 prepared the ground. Weeks 9–11 planted the courtyards. Elise Brandt set irrigation so the grasses and the sensory garden could be watered on a schedule the hospital could live with. Marcus Delgado kept the crew movements inside the weeks the survey had set.

After the handover walk

The handover walk was in week 12. Hospital staff walked the 3 courtyards with the crew, including the sensory garden, and Samuel Quist took aftercare from that day. Aftercare ran 24 months, the length written into every planting contract. A courtyard is not a street tree, so the record we keep is not a tree count. It is the courtyards themselves.

After 24 months, 3 of 3 courtyards were established. The sensory garden is inside that record, not a fourth site. Benches stayed in use. Grasses stayed in the planting plan. We do not add a claim about patients or about recovery. The case says the 3 courtyards were planted in 2023 and were established after 24 months, which is the whole of the result we state.

pages.title: Fraser Street renewal
pages.content:
Fraser Streetrenewal

Fraser Street renewal, in 2025, planted 112 street trees along 1.2 km in Metro Vancouver. After 24 months, 109 of 112 trees were established.

Case facts

Case facts

Client type: civic street. Place: Metro Vancouver. Year: 2025. Scope: 1.2 km and 112 street trees. After 24 months, 109 of 112 street trees were established. The job followed site survey, planting plan, ground preparation, planting, handover walk and 24 months of seasonal aftercare. Tom Okafor led the planting crew. Priya Raman checked the trees and the later establishment count. Samuel Quist coordinated aftercare. The ring on this case is the tree count: 109 of 112 established after 24 months.

109 of 112

Established after 24 months

1.2 km, 112 street trees

A kilometre of street trees

Fraser Street renewal planted a civic street in Metro Vancouver in 2025. The scope was 1.2 km and 112 street trees, set along a renewed street with a planted median. Weeks 1–2 were the site survey. The crew measured pits along the length, not a single forecourt, and the count of 112 came from that measuring. Weeks 3–5 were the planting plan. Hana Mori-Ellis wrote it to the company policies: 60% native or adapted species, and 80% of planting stock grown within 150 km.

Weeks 6–8 were ground preparation along the median and the pits. Weeks 9–11 were planting. Tom Okafor’s crew set the trees. Each street tree was planted with a guard, in the way our street-tree work is specified. Priya Raman checked stake and clearance as the pits were closed. The length stayed 1.2 km.

Establishment after 24 months

Week 12 was the handover walk down the planted street. Samuel Quist then coordinated seasonal aftercare for 24 months, including the 2 seasons of watering that belong with street trees. Priya Raman recorded establishment at the end of that period. The case record shows 109 of 112 street trees established after 24 months.

The three trees outside the count stay inside the same record. We state 109 of 112, not a rounded claim and not a forecast for the next kilometre. Fraser Street is the longest of the three jobs we show: a college forecourt in 2024, a hospital in 2023, and this 1.2 km street in 2025. The sequence of stages did not change because the site was a street. Survey, plan, preparation, planting, handover, aftercare.

pages.title: Process
pages.content:
Twelve weeks,then 24 months

A planting contract moves through six stages, from the first measurement to 24 months of aftercare. The weeks below are the weeks we schedule.

Six stages

From the first tape to month 24

Week 1–2

Site survey

Every planting contract starts with a site survey in weeks 1–2.

Week 3–5

Planting plan

Hana Mori-Ellis writes the planting plan in weeks 3–5.

Week 6–8

Ground preparation

Ground preparation runs in weeks 6–8.

Week 9–11

Planting

Planting runs in weeks 9–11 under Tom Okafor, crew lead for planting.

Week 12

Handover walk

Week 12 is the handover walk.

24 months

Seasonal aftercare

Seasonal aftercare runs for 24 months after the handover walk.

01

Site survey, weeks 1–2

Every planting contract starts with a site survey in weeks 1–2. The starting price is $1,200 CAD, and it includes the planting plan that follows. On site, two surveyors measure the tree pits, the paving edges and the room the canopy will need. A tape and a written record are the tools.

The notes cover campuses, hospital courtyards and civic streets the same way. Marcus Delgado uses them to hold the later weeks to a crew schedule. No tree is ordered in this stage. If you are booking now, winter planting slots for 2027 open with this survey, not with a shovel.

02

Planting plan, weeks 3–5

Hana Mori-Ellis writes the planting plan in weeks 3–5. She is the founder and the landscape architect. The plan names what goes in each pit, bed, courtyard or planter, and it has to clear two policies before we call it finished. 60% of the species are native or adapted.

80% of the planting stock will be grown within 150 km. Elise Brandt reads the plan where the job includes irrigation, a green roof or planters. The plan is also where quantities meet the starting prices, so a street tree, a monthly campus ground or a green roof can be counted before week 6. You walk the plan with us before preparation begins.

03

Ground preparation, weeks 6–8

Ground preparation runs in weeks 6–8. Pits are opened to the sizes measured in the survey. Beds are shaped. On a green roof or in planters, this is when drainage and soil go in, priced from $145 CAD per m², with Elise Brandt leading.

On a street, preparation is the pit and the paving edge, ready for a guard. On a campus or a hospital courtyard, it is the ground up to the area surveyed, whether that is a forecourt of 1,800 m² or 3 courtyards. Marcus Delgado keeps this stage inside its weeks so planting is not pushed into a guess. We do not plant into ground that skipped this step.

04

Planting, weeks 9–11

Planting runs in weeks 9–11 under Tom Okafor, crew lead for planting. Street trees are set with a guard. The street tree rate starts at $680 CAD per tree and includes the guard and 2 seasons of watering. Priya Raman, arborist, checks species against the plan, then stake and clearance, before the crew leaves the pit.

Campus forecourts and hospital courtyards are planted in these same weeks. The Northshore count was 64 trees. The Fraser Street count was 112. Both passed through this stage, three weeks, one crew lead, the plan from weeks 3–5 unchanged at the pit.

05

Handover walk, week 12

Week 12 is the handover walk. We walk the site with the client: every pit, the beds, the courtyards or the roof planters, against the plan. This is a working walk, not a ceremony. Questions about stakes, watering and access are answered on the ground.

Samuel Quist is there because he coordinates what happens next. The client leaves with the plan and with a named aftercare contact. Planting is complete at the end of this week. The contract is not. Every planting contract continues for 24 months, and the walk is the point where that period starts.

06

Seasonal aftercare, 24 months

Seasonal aftercare runs for 24 months after the handover walk. Samuel Quist coordinates it. A seasonal aftercare visit starts at $420 CAD. Street trees carry 2 seasons of watering inside the $680 CAD tree price.

Winter pruning, when a tree needs it, starts at $1,950 CAD per day for a crew of 3, with Priya Raman. At the end of 24 months we record establishment. The records we already hold are 62 of 64 trees at Northshore College, 3 of 3 courtyards at Riverside General Hospital, and 109 of 112 street trees on Fraser Street. Those counts are the aftercare result, written per case.

Winter planting slots for 2027 are open.

pages.title: Aftercare
pages.content:
Aftercare for24 months

Every planting contract includes 24 months of aftercare, coordinated from handover. The year splits into four seasons of visits, watering and winter work.

24 months on every planting contract

Aftercare at Daichi Landscapes runs for 24 months on every planting contract. It starts at the handover walk in week 12, and Samuel Quist coordinates it from the yard. The 24 months are company policy, stated the same way on a college, a hospital and a street. A seasonal aftercare visit starts at $420 CAD.

We record establishment at the end of the period. Northshore College forecourt, planted in 2024, shows 62 of 64 trees established. Riverside General Hospital, completed in 2023, shows 3 of 3 courtyards established. Fraser Street renewal, planted in 2025, shows 109 of 112 street trees established.

24 months

The year in four seasons

Mar–May

Spring

Spring is when new planting and the first care of last year’s trees overlap. Street trees planted under the $680 CAD rate carry 2 seasons of watering, and spring is when that watering is checked, stakes included. Samuel Quist lines up the seasonal visits, from $420 CAD, on campuses, courtyards and streets that are already in their 24 months. Forecourts that flower in spring, with seating out and trees in leaf, are walked so the crew sees what winter left. New work still begins with a survey. Spring does not skip weeks 1–2 just because the ground looks ready.

Jun–Aug

Summer

Summer care is watering and irrigation. The 2 seasons of watering included with a street tree are there for this part of the year as well as spring. Elise Brandt’s irrigation lines, in beds, planters and green roofs, are checked while they are actually running. A green roof installed from $145 CAD per m² needs that check as much as a courtyard does. Campus grounds on a monthly maintenance price, from $3,400 CAD up to 2 ha, are kept in use through the summer rather than closed for the crew. Visits stay on Samuel Quist’s list. We add a visit when the plan calls for one, at the $420 CAD rate.

Sep–Nov

Autumn

Autumn is the season between watering and pruning. Aftercare visits look at how the year’s planting has taken before growth slows: stakes, ties, and trees that need a note before winter. Samuel Quist books those visits across the contracts that are still inside their 24 months. Priya Raman reads the notes that will matter for winter pruning. Campus and hospital grounds stay open. A civic street does too. Autumn is also when a client can book the next survey. The planting plan that Hana Mori-Ellis writes in weeks 3–5 can be ready before a winter slot, including the slots open for 2027.

Dec–Feb

Winter

Winter is pruning season, and it can be planting season. Winter pruning starts at $1,950 CAD per day for a crew of 3. Priya Raman directs the cuts. The day rate is how a dormant tree on a campus, in a courtyard or on a street is handled inside aftercare. Winter planting slots for 2027 are open. A slot still begins with the site survey in weeks 1–2, at the $1,200 CAD starting price, and still ends its first year at the week 12 handover before the 24 months begin. The yard is not a Sunday operation. Saturday 8:00–12:00 is for pickups only.

Who you hear from

Samuel Quist is the aftercare coordinator and the person who schedules the 24 months. Priya Raman is the arborist on pruning and on establishment counts. Elise Brandt is the person on irrigation when summer asks a question about a line, a planter or a green roof.

You reach the yard at +1 604 555 0148 or hello@daichi-landscapes.example, Monday to Friday, 7:00–17:00. The office is Unit 4, 210 Mill Creek Road, Vancouver, BC V5Y 1Z3, Canada. Bring the site and the year it was planted. We will match it to the contract and to the 24-month record.

Ask for a site survey →

Winter planting slots for 2027 are open.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
About DaichiLandscapes

Daichi Landscapes Ltd. has planted for campuses, hospitals and civic streets in Metro Vancouver since 2009. The yard is in Vancouver, and the crew numbers 28.

Since 2009

Founded in 2009

Daichi Landscapes Ltd. was founded in 2009 by Hana Mori-Ellis, landscape architect. The company plants and maintains campuses, hospitals and civic streets across Metro Vancouver. The yard and office are at Unit 4, 210 Mill Creek Road, Vancouver, BC V5Y 1Z3, Canada. From the start the work has been the same shape it is now: a survey, a planting plan, preparation, planting, a handover walk and aftercare.

Hana still writes the plans. The phone is +1 604 555 0148 and the email is hello@daichi-landscapes.example. Hours are Monday to Friday, 7:00–17:00. Saturday 8:00–12:00 is yard pickups only. Sunday is closed.

From the hospital to the street

The recent record runs in order. In 2023 the company completed Riverside General Hospital: 3 courtyards and a sensory garden. After 24 months, 3 of 3 courtyards were established. In 2024 the company planted the Northshore College forecourt: 64 trees and 1,800 m². After 24 months, 62 of 64 trees were established.

In 2025 the company planted Fraser Street renewal: 1.2 km and 112 street trees. After 24 months, 109 of 112 trees were established. These are the three cases we write out in full. They are not a selected highlight reel with the counts removed. Each one is a planting contract with a public establishment figure.

A crew of 28

The crew is 28 people. Six of them lead the work you will meet by name. Hana Mori-Ellis is founder and landscape architect. Marcus Delgado is operations lead. Priya Raman is arborist. Tom Okafor is crew lead for planting.

Elise Brandt leads irrigation and green roofs. Samuel Quist is aftercare coordinator. The other hands are the planting crew, the preparation crew and the aftercare crew those six direct. We state the crew size here, as 28, so the scale of a week on site is clear. Marcus schedules that crew. The yard they leave from each morning is the Mill Creek Road address.

Meet the six leads →

Company policy

Policies we actually plant to

Three policies apply to every planting plan, whether the client is a college, a hospital or a street team. 80% of planting stock is grown within 150 km. 24 months of aftercare are included on every planting contract. 60% of the species in each plan are native or adapted. The policies are older than any one case and they were used on the 2023, 2024 and 2025 jobs alike. Starting prices sit beside them: survey and plan from $1,200 CAD, street trees from $680 CAD, campus maintenance from $3,400 CAD per month. Winter planting slots for 2027 are open if you want the next survey booked.

pages.title: Team
pages.content:
The peopleon the crew

Six people lead the work at Daichi Landscapes. You will meet them on the survey, the planting weeks or the aftercare that follows handover.

Founder, landscape architect

Hana Mori-Ellis

Hana Mori-Ellis, founder and landscape architect. She founded Daichi Landscapes Ltd. in 2009 and still writes every planting plan. In weeks 3–5 she sets species so that 60% are native or adapted, then returns for the handover walk in week 12. Her plans cover campuses, hospitals and civic streets across Metro Vancouver, from a single forecourt to a 1.2 km street.

Operations lead

Marcus Delgado

Marcus Delgado, operations lead. He turns the survey notes into a crew schedule and holds each job to its weeks: preparation in weeks 6–8, planting in weeks 9–11. He keeps campus, hospital and street work moving on weekdays, and he is the reason a courtyard can stay open while the crew is on site. The Monday to Friday yard hours, 7:00–17:00, are the frame he plans inside.

Arborist

Priya Raman

Priya Raman, arborist. She checks species, stake and clearance on street trees before a pit is closed, and she directs winter pruning with a crew of 3. At the end of 24 months she records establishment. The counts she stands behind are 62 of 64 trees at Northshore College, 3 of 3 courtyards at Riverside General Hospital, and 109 of 112 trees on Fraser Street.

Crew lead, planting

Tom Okafor

Tom Okafor, crew lead for planting. He runs the pit work in weeks 9–11 and sets the guards on street trees as they go in. Northshore College’s 64 trees and Fraser Street’s 112 street trees were planted under his lead. He works to the plan Hana wrote, on campuses and on civic streets, and he does not add trees once the surveyed count is in the ground.

Irrigation & green roofs

Elise Brandt

pages.content:
Careers onthe crew

Daichi Landscapes hires onto planting, irrigation and aftercare crews that already have named leads. The season follows the six stages of a planting contract.

Crew roles

Crew work sits with the six leads. Planting crews work under Tom Okafor in weeks 9–11, setting trees, guards and pits on campuses and civic streets. Ground preparation in weeks 6–8 feeds that planting. Irrigation and green-roof crews work under Elise Brandt, on lines, planters and roofs priced from $145 CAD per m².

Aftercare crews work under Samuel Quist for the 24 months after handover, including visits from $420 CAD. Winter pruning runs under Priya Raman as a crew of 3, from $1,950 CAD per day. Marcus Delgado schedules the weeks. Hana Mori-Ellis writes the plan the crew plants.

The working season

The year follows the contract, not a separate hiring calendar. Survey work is weeks 1–2. The plan is weeks 3–5. Preparation is weeks 6–8. Planting is weeks 9–11.

Handover is week 12. After that, aftercare runs 24 months, with watering across the 2 seasons included on street trees, visits through spring, summer and autumn, and pruning in winter. Winter planting slots for 2027 are open, which means survey and planting work continues into that winter for crews on the books. Yard and office hours are Monday to Friday, 7:00–17:00. Saturday 8:00–12:00 is yard pickups only, not a planting day. Sunday is closed.

How to enquire

Write to hello@daichi-landscapes.example or call +1 604 555 0148 and say which part of the crew you are asking about: planting, irrigation and green roofs, or aftercare. Name the season you can work. The yard and office are at Unit 4, 210 Mill Creek Road, Vancouver, BC V5Y 1Z3, Canada, and conversations happen Monday to Friday, 7:00–17:00.

We read enquiries against the roles above. There is no separate form and no posted wage on this page. You will hear back from the yard about the weeks Marcus has open.

posts.title: A planting contract, from the survey to month 24
posts.excerpt: A Daichi Landscapes planting contract runs from a two-week site survey through a written plan, planting, a handover walk, and 24 months of aftercare.
posts.content:
A planting contract with Daichi Landscapes Ltd. is a sequence of weeks, not a single day with a shovel. It starts when a campus, a hospital or a street team in Metro Vancouver asks for a site survey. The starting price for that survey and the planting plan is $1,200 CAD. Hana Mori-Ellis, founder and landscape architect, is responsible for the plan that comes out of the measuring. Nothing is ordered before those weeks are done.

Weeks 1–2 are the site survey. Two surveyors measure the pits, the paving edges and the room a young tree will need. They use a tape and write down what the ground is doing. On a campus forecourt that often means pale paving and steady foot traffic. On a street it means a run of pits rather than a single court. Marcus Delgado, operations lead, takes those notes and holds the later schedule still: ground preparation in weeks 6–8, planting in weeks 9–11. The survey is also how a winter slot is booked.

Weeks 3–5 are the planting plan. Two company policies have to be true before a tree is ordered. 60% of the species in the plan are native or adapted. 80% of the planting stock is grown within 150 km. A third policy sits at the far end of the contract: every planting contract includes 24 months of aftercare. Elise Brandt reads the plan wherever the job includes beds, planters or a green roof. Green roof and planter installation starts at $145 CAD per m². The plan is the moment quantities meet rates, so the client sees the count before preparation starts.

Planting is weeks 9–11, led by Tom Okafor. On a street, the starting price is $680 CAD per tree, including the guard and 2 seasons of watering. Priya Raman, arborist, checks the species against the plan, then the stake and the clearance, before the crew closes the pit. A campus ground runs on a different price once it is in care. Monthly maintenance for grounds up to 2 ha starts at $3,400 CAD. Marcus schedules that work so the place can stay open while the crew is there.

Week 12 is the handover walk. The client walks the pits, the beds or the courtyards with the crew, and the plan is checked on the ground. Samuel Quist takes aftercare from that day. A seasonal aftercare visit starts at $420 CAD. When the dormant season calls for structural cuts, winter pruning starts at $1,950 CAD per day for a crew of 3, with Priya directing. The 24 months are written into the contract at the beginning. Samuel is simply the person who carries them.

Three Metro Vancouver records show those months already completed. Northshore College forecourt, planted in 2024, was 64 trees and 1,800 m² of planting. After 24 months, 62 of 64 trees were established. Riverside General Hospital, completed in 2023, was 3 courtyards and a sensory garden. After 24 months, 3 of 3 courtyards were established. Fraser Street renewal, planted in 2025, was 1.2 km and 112 street trees. After 24 months, 109 of 112 trees were established. We state the case records as counts. They describe those three contracts.

Winter planting slots for 2027 are open. A survey booked for one of them is still weeks 1–2, still $1,200 CAD to start, and still followed by a plan, preparation, planting and a handover before the 24 months begin. The yard and office are at Unit 4, 210 Mill Creek Road, Vancouver, BC V5Y 1Z3, Canada. Monday to Friday the hours are 7:00–17:00. Saturday 8:00–12:00 is for yard pickups only. Sunday is closed. Call +1 604 555 0148 or write to hello@daichi-landscapes.example and ask for a site survey.

The people do not change with the season. Hana writes the plan. Marcus holds the weeks. Tom plants. Elise runs irrigation and green roofs. Priya checks the trees and the pruning. Samuel stays for the 24 months. That is the whole contract, from the first tape on site to the establishment count at the end.
